negative_snippets:
I visited Shree Delhi Gujarati Samaj Restaurant recently, hoping for authentic Gujarati flavors.

Honestly, don’t expect the real Gujarati taste here.

The thali looked decent, but the taste and quality were disappointing.

Flavors were bland, and nothing stood out as memorable.

The presentation was ordinary, not worth the hype.

For someone craving authentic Gujarati cuisine, I would recommend avoiding this place.

Overall, a completely underwhelming experience, especially for the price.

For solo traveler,  they only give a bed in dormitory, no separate room. Very cost effective.
Location is good. 700m from civil lines metro station. Kashimiri gate ISBT is also near.
Good Gujarati food is served in canteen.

I’m a Gujarati married to a Maharashtrian, and we visited this Gujarati Samaj for just a day to keep our luggage while we stepped out. Unfortunately, the experience was extremely disappointing.
Despite explaining our situation multiple times, we were denied entry simply because my husband isn’t Gujarati. They even questioned why my Aadhaar wasn’t updated with marriage details and insisted on speaking to my parents. The lady at the reception was rude and dismissive, even saying “you don’t look married” — which was completely uncalled for.
If a community space is meant for support, why create barriers that exclude people? What’s the point of having a Gujarati Samaj if you can’t even allow people to sit inside in a moment of need?
Definitely not recommended.
